rules.localIntel: Hand-curated from primary sources: each item was read at its own source on the date shown, states only what that source says, and quotes it where a quote is given. Where a source does not settle something (a winner, an end date) the item says not verified. Every link is re-checked on each daily build; an item whose source has gone is withdrawn until it is re-sourced. This is not a census: it lists the contracts, formularies and papers found and read, not every one that exists.
rules.frameworks: NHS Supply Chain framework names matching /\b(instrument decontamination|decontamination capital|tray wrap)\b/i. NHSSC names a framework after its clinical category, so the name is the key; the CBU category field is far too broad to filter on. COVERAGE LIMITS, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. THERE IS NO NHS SUPPLY CHAIN STERILE SERVICES CATEGORY. The three agreements above sit under Medical and Surgical Consumables and Diagnostic Equipment and Services, so no category filter could have produced this list and none was used: the frameworks are matched by subject and the rule is printed above so it can be judged. THIS PANEL SHARES ITS THREE FRAMEWORKS AND ITS TAGGED COMPANIES WITH INFECTION PREVENTION AND CONTROL, and nothing was taken off that page to build this one. A company tagged for sterile services in the Hub's supplier directory now appears on both, which is what a reprocessing supplier's market actually looks like. WHAT WAS REFUSED, AND WHAT IT COST. Bare 'autoclave' is not in the award filter, because 52 of its matches in this data are university and research-institute laboratory autoclaves with nothing in the title to separate them from a sterile services department; the cost here is near zero, because the genuine NHS autoclave rows carry 'SSD' or 'sterile services' in the same title and are caught by those: York's autoclave replacement project for endoscopy and sterile services is on this panel for that reason, and Bedfordshire's SSD autoclave cooling water chiller matches the rule but is a tender notice with no supplier rather than an award, so it is named here instead of counted. Bare 'reverse osmosis' and 'water treatment' were refused although reverse osmosis water IS sterile services plant: every hit in this data is renal dialysis water or an estates water-safety contract, and the renal page holds them. Bare 'instrument set' and 'loan kit' were refused because the only match is a theatre instrument rental, which this department processes but does not buy. HTM 01-01, THE STANDARD THIS DEPARTMENT IS RUN TO, HAS ZERO AWARD ROWS IN THIS DATA and is therefore not in the award filter at all; it is carried instead as a sourced and quoted policy item in the Hub's local intelligence store, read at NHS England's own Health Technical Memoranda index, so the standard is on the page without being faked into the procurement evidence. WHAT IS NOT HERE AT ALL: primary care dental decontamination, which is HTM 01-05 and a different service; decontamination of linen, which is HTM 01-04 and an estates contract in this data; environmental and room decontamination, which is infection prevention's Environmental Decontamination agreement and is not claimed here; the flexible and rigid endoscopes themselves, which are the scope and not the reprocessor and belong to the colorectal, gastrointestinal and endoscopy page; and mass casualty and CBRN decontamination, which is emergency preparedness. NO OPEN TENDER MATCHED TODAY, which means no notice on this patch is open for bidding in this feed, not that none was looked for.

rules.awards: Award-stage notices whose TITLE matches /\b(sterile services?|ssd|cssd|tssu|hsdu|sterilis\w*|steriliz\w*|decontaminat\w*|washer.?disinfect\w*|tray wrap|sterilisation wrap|instrument track\w*|instrument traceab\w*|traceability system|endoscope reprocess\w*|endoscope washer|automated endoscope|aer|ultrasonic bath|ultrasonic clean\w*|rigid containers?)\b/i and does not match /\b(laborator\w*|incubators?|dishwashers?|skin decontamination|decontamination lotion|rsdl|decontamination tent|asbestos|decontamination works|mattress\w*|bariatric|pressure area|patient handling|beds? and associated|deep clean\w*|vehicles?|dental|water treatment|reverse osmosis|water softeners?|linen|laundry|primary care)\b/i. The exclusion list exists because every pattern in it matched a real notice that was not this speciality. A CPV code beginning 33191 is recorded as corroboration where the feed carries one, but never admits a notice on its own: a notice carrying a basket of CPV codes is filed under all of them and bought under one. Buyer names are never matched on.
rules.openTenders: Notices still open for bidding, matched the same way. An empty list means no open notice on this patch today, not that none was looked for.
rules.drugTariff: No Drug Tariff part applies to this speciality. Part IX reimburses dressings and elastic hosiery (IXA), incontinence appliances (IXB), stoma appliances (IXC) and elastic hosiery (IXR); nothing on this patch is listed there, so the panel carries no tariff rather than reaching for the nearest part.
rules.directorySuppliers: Companies the Hub's own supplier directory files under this speciality, from the speciality labels on each company's directory record, resolved through speciality-label-map.json and speciality-map.json (Compare ids: ssd). They are labelled DIRECTORY-TAGGED because the tag is the Hub's filing of a company's range, not a procurement record: being listed here is not evidence of a contract or of volume, and the list is not a census of the market. A company that is also on this speciality's own frameworks is listed once, with the framework-named suppliers, and marked as also directory-tagged. WHERE A COMPANY IS ON ANOTHER FRAMEWORK: where a directory-tagged company is named on an NHS Supply Chain framework that is not counted as this speciality's, it is still listed, with that framework named against it and linked, so it is not lost from the page. 5 of the 5 listed here carry such a note. Framework names and links come from NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs as held in frameworks.json; an agreement the directory records from another buying organisation, such as an NHS Shared Business Services framework, is shown as the directory states it.
rules.gpPrescribing: No BNF section is mapped to this speciality, so no GP prescribing market is sized here rather than borrowing a neighbouring page's.
rules.mhraDsu: MHRA does not tag Drug Safety Updates to this area: no GOV.UK therapeutic-area facet maps to this speciality. That is a fact about how GOV.UK files them, not a finding that there are no safety updates relevant to it.

localIntel.title: Health Technical Memorandum 01-01: Management and decontamination of surgical instruments (medical devices) used in acute care
localIntel.date: First published 20 March 2013; all five parts last updated 8 July 2016; publication page updated 26 January 2024
localIntel.ends: No review or expiry date printed
localIntel.fact: The national guidance a sterile services department is run to in England. It is published in five parts: Part a management and provision (59 pages), Part b common elements (46 pages), Part c steam sterilization (99 pages), Part d washer-disinfectors (108 pages) and Part e alternatives to steam for the sterilization of reusable medical devices. Parts c and d are the two a capital equipment conversation turns on: the steriliser and the washer-disinfector each have their own part, with their own validation and testing requirements. NHS England classifies it under Topic: Estates, Publication type: Guidance.
localIntel.quote: Health Technical Memorandum (HTM) 01-01 explains the management of decontamination and the various ways to sterilize reusable medical devices used in acute care.
localIntel.use: Quote the part, not the memorandum. A buyer who asks what standard a washer-disinfector is validated to is asking about Part d; a steriliser question is Part c. The document is guidance published by NHS England, not a contract or a framework, and it applies in England only - Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland publish their own. It says nothing about who supplies the equipment, so it is never evidence that a company is approved.

localIntel.title: Health Technical Memorandum 01-06: Decontamination of flexible endoscopes
localIntel.date: First published 20 March 2013; all five parts last updated 30 June 2016; publication page updated 26 January 2024
localIntel.ends: No review or expiry date printed
localIntel.fact: The separate memorandum for flexible endoscope reprocessing, which is why an endoscopy decontamination tender is not an HTM 01-01 tender. Published in five parts: Part A policy and management (31 pages), Part B design and installation (37 pages), Part C operational management (72 pages), Part D validation and verification, including storage and drying cabinets (49 pages) and Part E testing methods (55 pages). Part D is the one that brings the drying cabinet inside the standard alongside the Automated Endoscope Reprocessor (AER).
localIntel.quote: The guidance consists of 5 parts: policy and management design and installation operational management validation and verification (including storage/drying cabinets) testing methods
localIntel.use: An Automated Endoscope Reprocessor (AER), its water testing and its drying cabinet all sit under this memorandum, not under HTM 01-01. Trusts that centralise endoscopy decontamination buy against it. England only, and it is guidance rather than a buying route.

localIntel.title: The decontamination Health Technical Memoranda, and which ones are NOT sterile services
localIntel.fact: NHS England groups four decontamination memoranda together. Two are this department's: HTM 01-01 (surgical instruments in acute care) and HTM 01-06 (flexible endoscopes). Two are NOT, and they are the reason an award search on the word decontamination returns work that belongs elsewhere: HTM 01-04 covers decontamination of linen for health and social care, last updated 9 June 2016, and HTM 01-05 covers decontamination in primary care dental practices, last updated 26 March 2013.
localIntel.quote: Health Technical Memorandum 01-05: decontamination in primary care dental practices
localIntel.use: Use this to place a tender before quoting a standard. A dental practice decontamination contract is HTM 01-05 and a laundry contract is HTM 01-04; neither is a sterile services department buying washer-disinfectors, and treating them as the same patch is the commonest way this market gets mis-sized.
